source: CAMIL GE-V-15 · Page 30 · Communications (rewritten for modern use)
notes: Rewritten at Leon's request. Nine words dropped as obsolete: 'pay phone', 'public phone',
'phone booth', 'phone book', 'receiver', 'cradle' and 'slot' are the anatomy of a payphone,
a machine a learner will never touch; 'cordless phone' names a distinction that stopped
mattering; 'fax' survives only in a few legal offices.
Twenty-one words added that the page predates: smartphone, tablet, charger, headphones,
wifi, website, browser, online, app, download, upload, password, username, text message,
chat, video call, social media, notification, screenshot, streaming, podcast.
E-MAIL normalised to 'email', which is how it is written now.
'screen' and 'television' also appear in The Living Room. Different areas.
EASY: this unit's vocabulary is abstract in a way the household pages are not.

area.name: Phones, Internet and Media
area.description: La comunicación de hoy: los aparatos, conectarse, los mensajes y las aplicaciones, y dónde se leen las noticias.

units.name: Devices
units.topic: The machines people use to work and communicate, and the two things you plug into them

units.name: Getting online
units.topic: How a device reaches the internet and how you identify yourself to a service. A username says who you are and a password proves it

units.name: Apps and messages
units.topic: The ways people write to each other now, and what a phone shows you when someone does

units.name: Files and streaming
units.topic: Moving a file to or from a device, and listening or watching without keeping a copy. Downloading brings a file to you, uploading sends one away

units.name: News and broadcast
units.topic: Where news comes from and how a newspaper is laid out. The headlines are the large titles, the front page is the first one
